paragraph: Hackensack has four real tiers, and the volume is in condos. Single-family closed 36 sales at a median of $650,000, mostly three-bedroom colonials and capes with two baths. A sale-to-list ratio of 1.00, 58 percent of homes selling above asking, and a median 21 days on market add up to competitive but not frenzied. Well-priced homes are moving, and you should expect competition on the good ones. Two- and three-families are the top tier at a median of $785,000 across 12 sales, most of them two-families, with a median 19.5 days on market. Condos and townhouses carry the volume, 82 sales at a median of $320,000, typically two-bedroom one-bath units spanning $200,000 to $667,500, so the median is the number to anchor on. At 34 percent above asking and 29 days on market, buyers have more room here than in the houses. Co-ops are the entry point at $201,000 across 8 sales, with a 43-day median and a ratio under 0.97, and they carry board approval, financing restrictions, and resale friction, which not every buyer is aware of going in. Single-family volume built from 4 closings in February to 8 and 9 in June and July, tracking the normal seasonal ramp, while condo medians bounced with the monthly mix rather than trending. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the rental income of a two-family, the low-maintenance lifestyle of a condo, or the lower price point of a co-op.
